baseline.note: BH on original BUSTED p-values (busted_results_v3 pipeline, n=4,974)

mechanism_A_anticonservative_compression.assumption: null p ~ U(0, 0.5); observed p deflated 2x relative to Uniform(0,1)
mechanism_A_anticonservative_compression.equivalent_to: BH at alpha=0.025 on original p (monotone transform preserves order)

mechanism_B_truncation_clipping.assumption: p > 0.5 values are truncated/clipped to the 0.5 boundary (point mass at 0.5)
mechanism_B_truncation_clipping.argument: BH critical values i/n*alpha <= alpha = 0.05 << 0.5, so the clipped point mass at 0.5 can never cross a BH threshold; and the relative order of all p<0.5 values is unchanged by clipping the upper tail, so the BH rejection set is identical to baseline.

conclusion: Under the truncation mechanism (B), the 1,690 BH-significant genes are entirely unchanged (1690 = 1,690): clipping cannot create or destroy rejections. Under the anti-conservative compression mechanism (A, null U(0,0.5)), correcting p* = 2p reduces BH significance from 1,690 to 1639 genes (97.0% of baseline). Which mechanism actually operates is determined empirically by the neutral simulation calibration (neutral_sim_calibration.json).
